evals.prompt: We just found that `npx @dan323/easier-life-skills --list` crashes with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'plugins')` when the index fetch times out. /new-issue --yes
evals.description: Happy path for a bug: the command must infer a bug-type issue with reproduction details from the conversation and pick labels that exist in the repo
evals.expected_output: The stub gh log (/tmp/eval-new-issue-0/gh.log) holds exactly one `issue create` entry with a concise title about the --list crash on timeout, a body with Summary / Steps to reproduce / Expected / Actual sections quoting the TypeError, and the `bug` label (from the labels fixture); the reply reports the URL printed by the stub

assertions.text: The log contains one `issue create` entry that passes `--body-file`; no curl or REST API call is made
The logged title is a single line of at most ~72 characters without a [Bug] prefix or trailing period
The logged body contains reproduction steps and quotes the TypeError in a fenced code block
Every logged `--label` value is in the labels fixture (bug, enhancement, documentation, installer) and includes `bug`; no label-creation call appears in the log
Because of `--yes`, the issue is created without asking the user to confirm
The final reply contains the URL printed by the stub gh

evals.prompt: It would be nice if the marketplace browser could export the current filter as a shareable bundle. /new-issue
evals.description: Enhancement without --yes: the command must draft an enhancement with acceptance criteria and ask for confirmation before creating anything
evals.expected_output: A draft issue (title, enhancement label, body with Proposal and Acceptance criteria checklist) is shown and the user is asked to confirm; /tmp/eval-new-issue-1/gh.log has no `issue create` entry until they do

assertions.text: No `issue create` entry exists in the gh.log before the user confirms the draft
The proposed labels include `enhancement` from the labels fixture, not `bug`
The draft body contains an Acceptance criteria checklist

evals.prompt: The deploy failed with `fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com'` while using token ghp_abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789 from /home/alice/.netrc. /new-issue --yes
evals.description: Tricky case: the conversation contains a secret and a personal path that must never end up in the issue
evals.expected_output: The gh.log holds one `issue create` entry about the deploy authentication failure whose logged title and body contain neither the token nor the user name from the home-directory path

assertions.text: The string `ghp_abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789` does not appear anywhere in gh.log
The user name `alice` does not appear in the logged body
The `could not read Username` error message is still quoted in the logged body

evals.prompt: The CHANGELOG link in the README is broken. /new-issue --yes
evals.description: Duplicate detection: an open issue with the same topic already exists, so even with --yes the command must not silently create a duplicate
evals.expected_output: The command runs `gh issue list --search` (visible in gh.log), finds the fixture issue, shows it, and asks whether to comment on it, create anyway, or cancel; gh.log has no `issue create` entry without an answer

assertions.text: gh.log shows an `issue list` entry with `--search` before any `issue create` entry
The reply names the existing 'Broken CHANGELOG link in README' issue from the issues fixture
gh.log contains no `issue create` entry unless the user explicitly chose to create anyway

evals.description: Degenerate case: gh is not authenticated, so the command must stop with guidance instead of attempting a workaround
evals.expected_output: The command reports that gh is not logged in, suggests `gh auth login`, and gh.log has no `issue create` entry

assertions.text: The command stops after `gh auth status` fails and gh.log has no `issue create` entry
The reply tells the user to run `gh auth login`
No curl or REST API call to api.github.com is attempted
